events.note: Sow late March, 6–8 weeks before planting out — earlier just makes leggy plants. Warm house; the conservatory's still too cold.
Early April at the latest — still in time for the greenhouse move.
Into the unheated greenhouse once nights stay above ~10°C there — usually late May, early June in a cold spring. Bury the stem deep.
Ripening fast in the greenhouse.
Pick everything before the greenhouse gets frost (often late September). Green ones ripen indoors.
Longest season of all — germinate, then keep in the warm house.
Last chance to start if you didn't in January — warm-lovers, keep them in the house.
Early June, once the greenhouse stays warm at night — chillies sulk below ~12°C.
First fruits ripening.
Pick everything remaining before the greenhouse gets frost.
Start from February — a long season, but they don't need a January start like chillies.
Last chance to start — warm-lovers, keep them in the house.
Early June, once the greenhouse stays warm at night.
First peppers — pick some green to keep the plant setting more.
Pick everything remaining before the greenhouse gets frost.
Sow late April, 3–4 weeks before planting out; warm-lovers, so germinate and grow on in the warm house.
Early June — cucumbers are the most cold-sensitive crop here. Give them strings to climb.
Pick regularly to keep them coming.
Start late April, 4 weeks before planting out.
Plant out early June, after the frost risk, once hardened off. Fleece for the first week.
Cut before the first frost (often late September), with a long stalk. Cure indoors somewhere warm for 1–2 weeks — the autumn sun is too weak.
Start late April with the pumpkins.
Plant out early June, after the frost risk, once hardened off. Fleece for the first week.
Summer squash from August — pick small and often.
Cut winter squash before the first frost. Cure indoors somewhere warm for 1–2 weeks.
Sow from seed for big bulbs by late summer — germinate warm, then grow on cool & bright in the conservatory so they don't get leggy.
Continue sowing; germinate warm, grow on cool in the conservatory.
Late April to mid May, once the soil has thawed — plant out seedlings, or push in sets with tips just showing.
Overwintering sets — early September so they root before the freeze. Riskier than garlic; only with reliable snow cover.
Use as they size up.
Lift when the tops fall over; cure somewhere dry and airy until the skins are papery.
From late April, once the soil has thawed — a short row every 3–4 weeks.
Pull as needed, about 8–10 weeks after sowing.
Sow in modules; germinate warm, then move to the conservatory to keep them sturdy.
Continue sowing; grow on cool in the conservatory.
Plant out late May to end of June — drop into deep dibbed holes and water in. Later and they run out of season.
Lift as needed. Leeks take frost, but lift the rest before the ground freezes solid (usually November).
Late September — gives the cloves time to root before the freeze.
Early October at the latest — cloves pointy end up, 5cm deep, then mulch.
Snap off the flower stalks (scapes) to boost bulb size — and eat them.
Lift late July to early August when the lower leaves yellow. Cure somewhere dry and airy.
Early carrots — sow in a deep container in the conservatory. They hate being moved, so they grow on where they're sown.
Late April, once the soil has thawed — sow under fleece to keep carrot fly off.
Succession sow every few weeks for a steady supply.
Early July at the latest for autumn roots — later ones stay tiny.
Early carrots from the conservatory.
Pull as they size up.
Lift the rest before the ground freezes and store in boxes of damp sand.
Late April to May, once the soil has thawed — slow to germinate, so be patient and keep moist.
Sweeter after frost — but lift and store before the ground freezes hard (a thick straw mulch buys a few weeks).
Direct sow once the soil is ~8°C; thin clusters to one seedling.
Continue for autumn roots.
Early July only, for a late crop.
Golf-ball to tennis-ball size is sweetest.
Lift the rest before heavy frost and store in damp sand.
Sow direct in the frost-free conservatory — slow in the cold, but the first fresh crop of the year.
Sow direct in the conservatory now — outdoors is still frozen.
Late April, once the soil has thawed — quick 25–30 day crop; sow little and often.
Keep the succession going.
Small sowings only — long midsummer days and heat make radishes bolt and go woody. Part shade helps.
Best autumn sowing — shortening days, no bolting.
First radishes from the conservatory.
Pull about 4 weeks after sowing, before they go woody.
Direct sow for quick summer roots.
Sow for autumn roots and to store.
Pull golf-ball size for eating fresh; lift the rest before the ground freezes.
Fast and hardy — direct sow a short row every few weeks.
Pick at tennis-ball size, before they get woody.
Late April to May, once the snow has gone and the soil has thawed. Support with twiggy sticks.
Pick young and often to keep them producing.
Late April to May with twiggy support, once the soil has thawed.
Pick regularly for tender, sweet pods.
Very hardy — sow as soon as the soil has thawed. (Skip autumn sowing — they don't survive a Swedish winter.)
Best picked small and tender.
Frost-tender — wait for early June and soil above ~12°C.
Early July only — later sowings won't crop before the first frost.
Pick young and often; stop at the first frost.

Pick often while the pods are young; stop at the first frost.
Early June, soil above ~12°C — they need the whole season to dry.
Leave the pods to dry on the plant; pick before the first frost and finish drying indoors.

Best sowing as it cools.
